figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. The 1,5-hydride shift in the biosynthesis of 1 by isotopic
labeling. The upfield shifted triplet for C19 in the experiment with (E)-
(4-13C,4-2H)IPP confirms the hydride shift from C12 to C19. More
details are shown in Figure S4.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Biosynthesis of 1 by NfSS. A) Cyclization of GFPP to 1 (full arrows) and to shunt products obtained from enzyme variants (dashed
arrows). Modeling of NfSS with carbocationic intermediates are shown aside. Carbocationic intermediates are shown as yellow sticks with the
carbocation positions highlighted in magenta. B) GC–MS analyses of the products obtained from NfSS and its enzyme variants. For highly
productive enzyme variants the Y-axis is interrupted.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Biosynthesis of 2 by PbSS. A) Cyclization of GFPP to 2 (full arrows) and to shunt products obtained from enzyme variants (dashed
arrows). Modeling of PbSS with carbocationic intermediates are shown aside. Carbocationic intermediates are shown as yellow sticks with the
carbocation positions highlighted in magenta. B) GC–MS analyses of the products obtained from PbSS and its enzyme variants. For highly
productive enzyme variants the Y-axis is interrupted. The biosynthetic pathway of 17 is the same as that of 2, with the only exception of different
configurations at C18.
